# `timesheet` commands

## `timesheet copy-last`

The anchor's Copy Last Sheet: this week's sheet plus the rows of the person's last earlier timesheet (customer:job, item, class, billable, notes) without hours, ready to fill in and pass to `timesheet save`. Writes nothing.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |
| Required role | member |
| Capability | customer-work |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/timesheet.copy-last` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow timesheet copy-last --employee "Casey Worker" --week 2026-10-27 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "timesheet copy-last", "input": {"employee": "Casey Worker", "week": "2026-10-27"}, "company": "Company ID or name"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `employee` | `--employee` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Employee ID or name. Leave it out for your own: the employee your login is linked to (`clock link`), or, for an agent, its principal's. |
| `week` | `--week` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Any day of the week to show; this week by default. |

## `timesheet save`

Save one person's week: the whole sheet, each row a customer:job, service item, class, billable, notes and seven daily hours. Each row and day with hours is one time entry, created, corrected or withdrawn so the entries match the sheet exactly; a cell whose hours did not move writes nothing, so saving the same sheet twice changes nothing. Hours a posted sale carries stay billed: lowering a cell below them is refused (E_WORK_DEPENDENCY); more hours in a billed cell become a new entry. A row left out withdraws its time. An agent may save any employee's sheet, as its principal could. Posts nothing. Example: 8 hours on the Smith job yesterday is one row with 8 in that day.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | customer-work |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/timesheet.save` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow timesheet save --employee "Casey Worker" --week 2026-10-20 --rows '[{"customer": "Riverside Apartments", "item": "Mainline Clearing", "billable": true, "notes": "Main line", "hours": ["8", "7.5", null, null, null, null, null]}]' --reason "Casey's week" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "timesheet save", "input": {"employee": "Casey Worker", "week": "2026-10-20", "rows": [{"customer": "Riverside Apartments", "item": "Mainline Clearing", "billable": true, "notes": "Main line", "hours": ["8", "7.5", null, null, null, null, null]}]}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `employee` | `--employee` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Employee ID or name. Leave it out for your own: the employee your login is linked to (`clock link`), or, for an agent, its principal's. |
| `week` | `--week` | string | yes | no | — | Any day of the week being saved.; minimum length 10; maximum length 10; pattern "^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$" |
| `rows[].customer` | inside `--rows` JSON array | string | yes | no | — | Customer:job the time was worked for.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |
| `rows[].item` | inside `--rows` JSON array | string | yes | no | — | Service item the time is charged as.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |
| `rows[].class_id` | inside `--rows` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | Class, when classes are on. |
| `rows[].billable` | inside `--rows` JSON array | boolean | no | no | true | — |
| `rows[].notes` | inside `--rows` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | What was done; it becomes the invoice line description. |
| `rows[].hours` | inside `--rows` JSON array | array[string \| null] | yes | no | — | Seven cells, the first day of the week first. Decimal hours of up to six places: 8, 7.5 or 0.25. Empty or 0 is no time that day. |
| `expected_sheet_version` | `--expected-sheet-version` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The sheet_version `timesheet show` returned; refused if the week changed since. |

## `timesheet set-preferences`

Set the first day of the work week (monday by default), clock rounding (none, the default, or the nearest 6 or 15 minutes) and the maximum shift in hours (16 by default). Name only what changes. Time already recorded keeps its hours.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | customer-work |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/timesheet.set-preferences` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow timesheet set-preferences --clock-rounding 15 --reason "Round punches to the quarter hour" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "timesheet set-preferences", "input": {"clock_rounding": "15"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `week_start` | `--week-start` | literal["monday", "tuesday", "wednesday", "thursday", "friday", "saturday", "sunday"] \| null | no | yes | null | First day of the work week on timesheets (monday by default). |
| `clock_rounding` | `--clock-rounding` | literal["none", "6", "15"] \| null | no | yes | null | Round clocked time to the nearest 6 or 15 minutes, or not at all (none, the default). |
| `max_shift_hours` | `--max-shift-hours` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | Longest a clock may run (16 by default); a clock open longer must be closed with a stated end time. |

| `week_start` | literal["monday", "tuesday", "wednesday", "thursday", "friday", "saturday", "sunday"] | yes | no | — | — |
| `clock_rounding` | literal["none", "6", "15"] | yes | no | — | — |
| `max_shift_hours` | integer | yes | no | — | — |
| `version` | integer | yes | no | — | — |
| `changed` | boolean \| null | no | yes | null | — |

Example JSON output:

```json
{
  "changed": null,
  "clock_rounding": "none",
  "max_shift_hours": 1,
  "version": 1,
  "week_start": "monday"
}
```

## `timesheet show`

One person's work week as the anchor's Weekly Timesheet shows it: one row per customer:job, service item, class, billable and notes, hours for each day, totals by day and for the week. Each cell lists its time entries; a cell a posted sale carries is locked, with a note naming the sale. The week starts on the company work-week start (`timesheet preferences`). Leave employee out for your own sheet.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |
| Required role | member |
| Capability | customer-work |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/timesheet.show` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow timesheet show --employee "Casey Worker" --week 2026-10-20 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "timesheet show", "input": {"employee": "Casey Worker", "week": "2026-10-20"}, "company": "Company ID or name"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `employee` | `--employee` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Employee ID or name. Leave it out for your own: the employee your login is linked to (`clock link`), or, for an agent, its principal's. |
| `week` | `--week` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Any day of the week to show; this week by default. |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/timesheet.show`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |

### Output

| JSON field | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `employee_id` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `employee_name` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `week_start` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `week_end` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `week_start_day` | literal["monday", "tuesday", "wednesday", "thursday", "friday", "saturday", "sunday"] | yes | no | — | — |
| `days` | array[string] | yes | no | — | — |
| `rows` | array[object] | yes | no | — | — |
| `rows[].customer_id` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `rows[].customer_name` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `rows[].item_id` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `rows[].item_name` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `rows[].class_id` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | — |
| `rows[].class_name` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | — |
| `rows[].payroll_item` | NoneType | no | no | null | Reserved for payroll items; always null until payroll exists. |
| `rows[].billable` | boolean | yes | no | — | — |
| `rows[].notes` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | — |
| `rows[].hours` | array[string \| null] | yes | no | — | — |
| `rows[].total` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `rows[].cells` | array[object] | yes | no | — | — |
| `rows[].cells[].date` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `rows[].cells[].hours` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | — |
| `rows[].cells[].entries` | array[string] | yes | no | — | — |
| `rows[].cells[].locked` | boolean | yes | no | — | Some of these hours are billed: the cell may grow, but not drop below billed_hours. |
| `rows[].cells[].billed_hours` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `rows[].cells[].lock_note` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `rows[].locked` | boolean | yes | no | — | — |
| `day_totals` | array[string] | yes | no | — | — |
| `week_total` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `sheet_version` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `copied_from` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `lock_note` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |

Example JSON output:

```json
{

  "week_end": "value",

  "week_start_day": "monday",
  "week_total": "value"
}
```
